authoredNote: Written from the TypeScript family's contract (real-typescript-analyzer.ts: class heritage -> extends, implements_clause -> implements, a member the base or an in-file interface also declares -> overrides with the `${sub}.${member}` -> `${base}.${member}` endpoint) plus the SFC seam's two published rewrites (F8 re-points a delegated row's SOURCE at the one component identity; M59 #825 shifts its line by the block offset). No expectation value was copied from analyzer output.
rationale: Pins the positive half of this lane's `implements` and `overrides` verdicts. Both are RULED-BY-CORPUS — measured 0 occurrences of a class-with-superclass, a class-with-implements and an `override` modifier across 897 script blocks in 1,151 real .vue files (script/vue-fix/vue-construct-probe.ts) — and a ruling whose positive half is only a probe dies with the probe. This is the shape that proves the seam carries the delegate's class-heritage rows rather than dropping them, which is the claim the corpus cannot make. It is deliberately NOT a Vue construct: a class in a script block is ordinary TypeScript, so every row here is the DELEGATE's arriving through the seam, and the assertions that matter are the seam's: `sfcDelegated: true` on every row, the class-identity SOURCE (F8), and a line on the FILE's numbering rather than the script-relative one (M59 #825 — the script block starts on line 2 here, so an unshifted line would be 1 lower on every row).

forbidRelationships.comment: F19: `default` is a keyword, never a symbol. A NAMED default export (`export default class Widget`) resolves to `Widget` and ships; the anonymous object form publishes no exports row at all.
Shape declares `area`, not `render`: the interface arm must not invent the member it does not declare.
direction: the subclass overrides the base, never the reverse.
direction: the class implements the interface.
